sources.notes: Road height is sampled from the existing approximately 16 m terrain raster and compressed to a 0.5 m interpolation tolerance relative to those samples; this is not road-surface survey accuracy. Station distances use the midpoint of corresponding border stations, not an official length measurement. There is no saved GPS start gate; the simulation begins at the first trace coordinate. Curbs and bend labels are geometry-based illustrations, not extracted from imagery or verified real curb locations; widths, heights and colours are assumed. Banking is unknown and assumed zero. Source border coordinates retain their separate feature-level licence; invalid cross-sections are interpolated. Imagery is an external display resource subject to provider terms; no image bytes are included.

measurement.note: Native-image reviewed, RGB-assisted estimated pavement-edge readings on the pinned USDA NAIP image captured2022-06-24. Native pixel spacing is0.6m; the requested0.3m render adds no ground detail or positional accuracy. Contrast interval candidates only help locate transitions and are not confidence values. Original source geometry is retained. Unread right edge20, left edge50, the inner tree-shadowed bend near250, and unmarked junction openings interpolate between visible observations. Additional native reads at2,5,205,215,245,248,252,255,325 and332 refine the local proposal. The outer junction from source325 through5 uses short straight joins between observed points; its exact rounding remains estimated. Station10 starts the measurement grid; unnamed shared paving is an inferred corridor, not every connected apron. Direction and historical alignment remain draft, timing missing, curbs illustrative and banking unknown.

borderInference.note: Road-border estimates reconstructed directly from complete, sparse image measurements on the existing trace cross-sections. All intervals interpolate between image anchors; they are not automatic detections or a continuous edge survey. Every saved edge station and anchor requires pinned-image coverage during authoring. Isolated missing pixels inside the road are not filled or used as boundary evidence. Imagery resolution is not survey accuracy. These borders have not been formally verified.
